quote.text: The large print giveth, and the small print taketh away.
quote.author: Tom Waits, "Step Right Up," Small Change (1976)

stories.headline: A Line Is Drawn Through Hormuz
stories.dek: Iran says it has agreed with Oman on a new corridor for shipping through the strait — inbound traffic hugging Iran's coast, outbound near Oman. Western analysts read the same page and see the opposite of what Washington wanted: a de-escalation that leaves Tehran holding more of the water, not less. The joint statement is still in drafting; a bulker that burned on 3 August is not.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · The Relief Trade
stories.headline: A Record Bought on an Unsigned Truce
stories.dek: Oil is falling for a third straight session, gold has printed a record, and a global all-world portfolio sits near its high. The single force behind all of it is a Hormuz de-escalation that no one has yet signed — which is the clause the tape is choosing to ignore.

stories.headline: The Fine Print
stories.dek: History's great transfers of power rarely happened at the podium. They happened in a clause — a line on a map, a sentence in a treaty, a field-of-use restriction most people never read. A week of announcements, and the deals were all in the small print.

stories.headline: A Parade Now, the Policy in a Fortnight
stories.dek: National Day returns to the National Stadium on Sunday with an indoor drone show and an off-year's quiet confidence. The announcement that will actually shape a household lands two weeks later, when the Prime Minister rises at ITE College Central.

stories.headline: The Index Dips, the Ceiling Rises
stories.dek: The HDB resale index has fallen for a second straight quarter — its first back-to-back decline in nearly seven years. In the same three months, a record number of flats changed hands above a million dollars. Both are true; the headline hides the clause.

stories.headline: Huawei's Own Silicon Reaches the Cloud
stories.dek: The Ascend 950DT — Huawei's answer to the training chips it can no longer import — arrives on Huawei Cloud this month, a quarter ahead of hardware anyone can hold. The claim is compute independence; the fine print is that every number in it is Huawei's own.

stories.headline: Built for a Decade, Deaf to Your House
stories.dek: Marshall's Stanmore IV is the buy-once home speaker done properly — wood cabinet, real amplification, a decade's worth of build. The review wave landed in early August with one recurring caveat, and for a Lutron-and-Home-Assistant household it is the whole story: it speaks only Bluetooth.

stories.headline: A Dive Watch Sold Pre-Worn
stories.dek: DOXA and Hodinkee have revived a rare 1969 Swiss military diver as the SUB Army 200T — 39mm, US$2,000, 250 pieces. Its cleverest and most contested detail is a raw steel case built to look already aged. You are buying, in part, a life the watch has not lived.

stories.headline: The Biggest Opening, the Weakest Reviews
stories.dek: Spider-Man: Brand New Day took the largest domestic weekend in history and crossed a billion dollars in six days. It is also the lowest-rated of Tom Holland's four Spider-Man films. The gap between the receipts and the reviews is the week's most honest number.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · The Ban, Year One
stories.headline: The Toughest Phone Law, and Its Loophole
stories.dek: Eight months into Australia's world-first under-16 social-media ban, the first peer-reviewed look finds that more than 85% of the children it targets are still on the platforms. The law's weakest clause is the one that decides everything: it takes the child's word for their age.

stories.headline: The Hundred-Hour Contract
stories.dek: Gloomhaven is a board game the size and weight of a legal deposition, and the deal it asks a group of friends to sign is unusually explicit: ninety-five scenarios, a hundred hours, permanent changes you can't take back. This is the on-ramp to the strangest commitment in the hobby.

stories.headline: Training That Reaches the Transcriptome
stories.dek: A Dutch study finds that in lifelong-trained older muscle, roughly half the molecular signatures of ageing simply aren't there. It is the most biomarker-flavoured longevity result of the summer — and the fine print, as ever, is in the study design.

stories.headline: What's Worth Booking
stories.dek: A dense autumn to plan around: Singapore's first F1 Sprint weekend with a stadium's worth of pop beside it, and a Tokyo sumo basho whose good seats vanish the morning they go on sale — this Saturday.
